working_memory.text: The Dunmere cider press, a hand-turned screw press built from oak beams in the 1850s, has been rebuilt and will press apples again this autumn for the first time in forty years. Volunteers replaced the rotten base beam with seasoned oak from a fallen tree on the estate and re-cut the screw thread by hand. Anyone with surplus apples can bring them on the two pressing days and take juice home in exchange. The press sits in a barn beside the estate's walled garden.
